main:1.text: Chapter 1 is the first chapter in the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing the chapter for the first time unlocks the "Mission Underway" in-game challenge. The chapter opens with a scene depicting black-robed individuals performing what seems to be sacrificial ritual on a woman. Via narration by Leon Scott Kennedy, we are told that it has been six years since the Raccoon City Incident.

main:2.text: Chapter 2 is the second chapter in the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing the chapter for the first time unlocks the "Gift in the Blood" in-game challenge. Leon has a nightmare about a strange, robed man who laments about the fact that Leon now too is harboring some kind of "blessing". After waking up, he finds himself locked in a room with the survivor he rescued, who introduces himself as Luis Serra Navarro.

main:3.text: Chapter 3 is the third chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing the chapter for the first time unlocks the "Infested Inside" in-game challenge. After the confrontation with Méndez, Leon receives the intel he requested about Luis from Hunnigan.

main:4.text: Chapter 4 is the fourth chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing the chapter for the first time unlocks the "The First Daughter" in-game challenge. Leon once again experiences the same nightmare, the leader of the cult this time telling Leon that he too shall share in the cult's "holy blessing" by daybreak.

main:5.text: Chapter 5 is the fifth chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing the chapter for the first time unlocks the "Glimmer of Hope" in-game challenge. Having assured Ashley that, he's an agent entrusted by her father to rescue her and get her home safe, Ashley agrees to go with Leon. Once the two escape from the church, Leon informs Hunnigan of the recent development, who informs him that an evac.

main:6.text: Chapter 6 is the sixth chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completion of this chapter for the first time unlocks the "Farewell, Village of Terror" in-game challenge. Luis meets up with Ada Wong by a cliff, who, having survived the Raccoon City Incident, is now in the village on a mission.

main:7.text: Chapter 7 is the seventh chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completion of this chapter for the first time unlocks the "Shadows Within" in-game challenge. Having retreated to Salazar Castle, Leon is contacted by Luis, who tells the pair to meet him at the courtyard, claiming that he has medicine to help suppress their Plaga infections.

main:8.text: Chapter 8 is the eight chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing this chapter for the first time unlocks the "Reunited" in-game challenge. After getting separated from Ashley, Leon informs Hunnigan about the situation, but the radio connection between the two breaks as a result of the line getting jacked. Having lost his remote assistance, Leon sets out to find Ashley.

main:9.text: Chapter 9 is  the ninth chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Beating this chapter unlocks the "Dire Situation" in-game award. Leon contacts Luis, demanding to know his whereabouts, to which Luis replies that he "messed up" and asks Leon to come find him in the ballroom. Leon and Ashley make their way through the hedge maze, infested with violent Colmillos, the same which Leon encountered in the village.

main:10.text: Chapter 10 is the tenth chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing this chapter for the first time unlocks the "The Depths of Hell" in-game challenge.

main:11.text: Chapter 11 is the eleventh chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing this chapter for the first time unlocks the "Adios, Caballero" in-game award. Having injected himself with the Plaga suppressant, which slows down the rate of the Plaga's growth, Leon is filled with a new determination to rescue Ashley. He and Luis then begin their journey to escape from the underground mines.

main:12.text: Chapter 12 is the twelfth chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing this chapter for the first time unlocks the "Overthrowing the Castle" in-game challenge. Holding the key entrusted to him by Luis, Leon makes his way back to the castle, vowing to make sure Krauser pays for his actions. En route, he is contacted by Ada, who tells him that Salazar's henchmen have taken Ashley to the clock tower.

main:13.text: Chapter 13 is the thirteenth chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing this chapter for the first time unlocks the "Another Rescue" in-game challenge. As Ada rides the jet-ski The Island, the cult's stronghold, Leon is strangely silent. He then talks about how the Raccoon City incident changed everything, and how trying to save just one person results in the deaths of so many others.

main:14.text: Chapter 14 is the fourteenth chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing this chapter for the first time unlocks the "Letting Go of the Past" in-game challenge. As Ashley regains consciousness, Leon informs her about Luis' death. With no more time to lose, the two get going again.

main:15.text: Chapter 15 is the fifteenth chapter in the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing this chapter for the first time unlocks the "I'll Do My Job" in-game challenge. Leaving the ruins, Leon's arrives at the island's military base, where they've set up turrets, traps, explosives and the soldiers are armed to the teeth.

main:16.text: Chapter 16 is the sixteenth and final chapter of the Resident Evil 4 remake. Completing this chapter for the first time unlocks the "Darkest Before Dawn" in-game challenge, as well as several in-game unlocks (which vary depending on the difficulty the game is finished on), most notably Professional Difficulty.

boss:1.text: Del Lago (デルラゴ, deru-rago?) (Spanish, literally meaning From the Lake) was a massive Plaga-infected amphibian that lived in a lake in Valdelobos. One of the earlier Plaga experiments by Los Iluminados, Del Lago, was a salamander that became host to a parasite. The organism reacted to its small host by mutating it, increasing its size considerably.

boss:2.text: El Gigante (/ˈel xiˈɣãn̪t̪e) (lt. "The Giant" in Spanish) is the name of a group of human-based Bio Organic Weapons produced by Los Iluminados. They stand four times taller than the average human and have increased strength and durability.

boss:3.text: Father Bitores Méndez (ビトレス・メンデス, Bitoresu Mendesu?) was a Catholic priest who ran the church in Valdelobos, an isolated mountainous region of Spain, and chief of the local village. Méndez fell to the influence of bio-weapons developer and terrorist Osmund Saddler, who converted people to his cult as a means of control. Fr. Méndez led the initial hunt for USSTRATCOM agent Leon S. Kennedy, Ashley Graham, Dr.

boss:4.text: The Verdugos, Spanish for "Executioner," also known as U-III in the reimagining, were B.O.W.s created by Los Iluminados to serve as personal bodyguards or the right-hand men of Ramón Salazar. A Verdugo was created by a fusion of human and insect DNA, completely controlled by a Plaga.[excerpt 1] Two Verdugos served as Ramón Salazar's bodyguards.

boss:5.text: Ramón Salazar (ラモン・サラザール, Ramon Sarazāru?) was a Spanish nobleman from Valdelobos. A descendent of the 15th century noble warrior, Gregorio Salazar I, Ramón inherited the position of castellano alongside his peerage, a duty more important to the family than the peerage itself.

boss:6.text: For other characters named "Jack" see Jack (disambiguation) Major Jack Krauser (ジャック・クラウザー, Jakku Kurauzā?) was an agent for the 3rd Organization during the War on Terror, and a supporter of Dr. Albert Wesker. Previously a soldier within USSOCOM known as "Silverdax," he was forced into retirement after a 2002 mission to South America with USSTRATCOM agent Leon S. Kennedy.

boss:7.text: Lord Osmund Saddler (オズムンド・サドラー, Ozumundo Sadorā?) was the leader of Los Iluminados, a neopagan cult and paramilitary organisation. He was a bio-weapons research chief who resided in an isolated Spanish region. In the early 2000s, Saddler's leadership ensured the cult's dominance in the region through the weaponisation of the mind-controlling Plaga parasites to suit his plans for world domination.
